expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: The numbers have been great for Shough so far, and the offense is humming. DraftKings fell asleep on this pricing. He is one of the best values on the slate this week.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I was high on Tyler Shough ($5,400 DK / $7,500 FD) coming into the year, but even I didn't see this level of production coming through two games. Nearly all of it has come in his last six quarters (plus OT). His 24 FPPG is already strong for the price, but his 31 XFPPG suggests there's still more in the tank. The Saints are playing the league's fastest pace, and now get a home opener against a Raiders defense I'm not buying as legitimate. I could see a shootout here.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Tyler Shough comes in as a very PT/$ friendly QB for cash games this week. Coming into week 3, Shough has completed 62 of 90 passes for 662 yards and 4 TDs (adding one TD on the ground as well).

players.notes: Playing in the fastest-paced offense with high pass volume at home.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: The price tag is high on both sites, as it should be. But on FanDuel, we have the luxury of being able to build around Josh Allen with players who are actually pretty solid due to some pricing mistakes over there.

players.notes: Elite pass volume in a game with a high 49.5 implied total.
Strong passing role and implied team total in a favorable spot.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Geno Smith is one of my favorite cheaper QB options on DK as Garrett Wilson is my favorite WR to pair him with.   I could see Smith airing it out quite a bit against a Lions secondary that is especially depleted at safety.  Wilson has elite upside and is just $6.3K on DK and you can get the cheaper WR option in Adonai Mitchell for just $4.3, making this a cheaper stack to build around allowing you to pay up for some of the higher priced players in great positions this week.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Dirt cheap on both sites and should be unowned in GPPs. Very much like last week, Geno should be forced to throw the ball 40 times in one of the highest total games on the slate. His main receiving weapons are also fairly priced, which makes stacking him very affordable and allows you to runback the expensive pieces for the Lions.

players.notes: Poised for heavy pass volume against a depleted secondary.
High pass-rate game environment with a massive 53.5 total.
Directing an explosive offense in a high-total matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Over the last three years, according to Fantasy Points, the Vikings have had the third-highest aDOT in the NFL against single-high coverage. That’s the primary coverage Tampa Bay plays, and the big-play upside is significant in this matchup.

players.notes: Dual-threat rushing floor and efficient passing volume.
Pass-heavy game script with a high 49.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Through two games, this Dallas defense has had no answers for running quarterbacks. Jaxson Dart had plenty of success in Week 1, and Jayden Daniels was well on his way to an easy 100-yard rushing game before injuring himself right before halftime. So if plays break down in Week 3, we're going to see Lamar use his legs quite a bit.

players.notes: Elite rushing floor in the highest game total on the slate.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Sometimes DFS doesn't need to be complicated. I faded Brock Purdy ($6,500 DK / $8,200 FD) last week despite a dream matchup, worried about a blowout — he still dropped 28 fantasy points anyway. He's in another great spot this week, as the Niners once again carry one of the slate's highest team totals (28), this time against a Cardinals defense I expect to finish bottom-10 by year's end. San Francisco ranks 3rd in PROE, and Purdy's legs keep adding value on top of his arm — his XFPPG is 4th-best among QBs.

players.notes: Leading a high-pace offense with a 28 implied team total.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Mahomes is the 3rd highest scoring QB on the year with a 28 point implied team total while also providing leverage on the incredibly popular KW3. I expect his DK/FD price tags will be much higher very soon.

players.notes: Commanding a high implied team total in a great matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Jahmyr Gibbs ($8,800 DK / $9,200 FD) is delivering exactly what we hoped for now that David Montgomery is in Houston. The bell-cow role suits him perfectly — he's averaging 29 fantasy points per game through two weeks, playing 77% of the snaps, and running a route on 55% of dropbacks. The numbers will say the Jets have been tough against the run, but they have faced the Titans and Packers, who have non-existent rushing attacks. There's no reason to fade Gibbs in Week 3.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Gibbs saw his role decrease in Week 2, following an overtime win, in a Thursday night game following a Sunday game. He still scored over 20 fantasy points that game. The role is almost too good to fail as long as Gibbs is healthy.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: The bellcow RB Jahmyr Gibbs gets a dream matchup with the Jets. While on paper the Jets look good against the run, they have yet to face the talent that is Gibbs. No player on the slate has as great of a floor as Gibbs, and should be a must have in cash games.

players.notes: Bell-cow role with heavy snap share and elite route participation.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: For the first time in his career, Jaylen Warren will be getting a start without a trusted backup (Najee/Gainwell never missed a game). Warren played a career-high 50 snaps last week; I think his workload will be unassailable here against CIN.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Warren has always had the talent to be a great fantasy asset if he saw increased usage. We should finally see that increased usage with Rico Dowdle out this week.

players.notes: Clear backfield control with an unassailable workload.
Heavy touch volume and goal-line control as the lead back.
Workhorse role with elite rushing volume in a high total.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Dolphins have been solid against the run through the first two weekends, but the Chiefs’ run blocking and usage of Walker outweigh what we’ve seen from Miami so far. I do expect Emmett Johnson to see some more work here, but if Walker gets 20 touches, he has the upside to score twice and clear 100 yards.

players.notes: Dominant snap share and heavy rushing volume as a favorite.
Strong rushing floor and heavy red-zone usage as a favorite.
Explosive pass-catching role and high-efficiency touches.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Montgomery has one elite game and one terrible game so far on the Texans. I'm expecting that volatility to continue. Against a Colts defense that has allowed the 2nd-most fantasy points to running backs so far this year, I'll bet on a bounce-back for Montgomery. It's a strong contrarian GPP play.

players.notes: Bounce-back spot against a defense struggling against backs.
Solid touch projection in a closely contested matchup.
Strong passing-game involvement and efficient rushing share.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: The Commanders have one of the worst secondaries in all of the NFL as CeeDee Lamb just had a field against them last week.  JSN is currently projected for only 11% ownership and I absolutely love this spot for him as he has been nothing short of spectacular to start the year.  It’s even better yet if we can get JSN at lower ownership.

players.notes: Elite target share and route participation as a heavy favorite.
Primary target in a high-volume passing offense.
High target volume in a fast-paced home environment.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Parker has the 2nd highest target share in the NFL with a top 5 yards per route run through 2 games. The Pats are not an ideal matchup, but he's way too cheap and should avoid Christian Gonzalez with most of his snaps coming from the slot.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Parker Washington is giving us JSN level usage with arguably a better quarterback and overall offensive efficiency. He is my favorite WR play of the slate on both DK and FD.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: The Patriots are far from an ideal matchup on paper, ranking 2nd in EPA allowed per dropback and 11th in fantasy points allowed to wideouts through two games. But dig a little deeper and the setup for Parker Washington ($6,000 DK / $7,100 FD) actually looks great. He runs nearly half his routes from the slot, keeping him away from Christian Gonzalez, and the Patriots have played man coverage at the 2nd highest rate in the league this season. Washington has a massive 57% target rate against man coverage, so expect him to get peppered with looks in this one.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Washington's salary and ownership are slowly catching up to what we're seeing from him this year. But we're still getting a discount on both.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Parker Washington continues to be underpriced given his usage entering Week 3. He should have a similar role on Sunday as he did last week, playing primarily from the slot, this time to avoid a matchup with Christian Gonzalez (this weeks version of Pat Surtain). Until they raise his price or make his ownership uncomfortable to play, he will be a staple in my lineups.

players.notes: High slot route rate avoids top corner in a heavy man scheme.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: McConkey was a priority for the Chargers offense early in Week 1. He has been limited by an injury, but he should be healthier with an extra week of recovery.

players.notes: Healthier with an expanded target role in the slot.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Playable in both cash and GPPs for me this week as he is a very safe runback for any Geno Smith team. ASB now has 19 receptions on 27 targets and 4 TDs entering this week. He continues to be Goffs main guy in the redzone outside of Gibbs.

players.notes: Elite target share and high route participation.
Deep route tree and high target ceiling as the clear WR1.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: I have nothing to back this up other than the fact that the Cowboys are a good passing offense and Baltimore looked susceptible through the air, at least in Week 2. But I have a hunch that after two bad weeks, the passing game will go through George Pickens this week in Brazil.

players.notes: Poised for increased target volume in a pass-heavy script.
Elite target share and deep route participation.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Panthers have the 4th highest PROE in the league, and the targets are extremely condensed to justa. few guys, with McMillan as the lead dog. Jalen Coker has put up better counting stats, but TMac has the same target share and the biggest air yards share on the team (40%). The Browns pass defense was torched by the Jags in Week One, and some missed throws, drops and weather made their week 2 seem better than it was. This is an exploitable unit, and TMac looks set for a big leap in year two, especially with Bryce Young playing really well to start the season, but they are drawing no ownership again this week. For TMac, Jalen Coker is also banged up and questionable to play, so we may see a larger target share this week as well.

players.notes: Massive air yards share and condensed targets as lead wideout.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Schultz is still a tremendous value on DK in particular this week as he saw 14 targets in their game against the Bengals with Nico Collins out.  Collins is doubtful to play once again and I would expect him to be heavily involved in the offense once again making him more like cheap WR option with heavy usage.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: With Collins ruled out again, Schultz becomes another elite play and a cash must have. Last week, he collected 12 of 14 catches for 140 yards. He also faces a Colts defense that continues to struggle vs TEs. Both their starting LBs have struggled in coverage, and they were just tormented by Kelce for 9-101-1.

players.notes: Heavy target volume operating as a primary receiver.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Gadsden showed flashes of the elite fantasy asset he can be when given the opportunity last year. With both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar out, he should get the opportunity the next few weeks. And the Chargers are likely going to need to throw to keep up with the Bills.

players.notes: Seam usage and increased route participation in a high total.
Elite route rate and consistent target volume in the offense.
Strong route participation and red-zone involvement.
Reliable seam targets and consistent route rate.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Kincaid has always been one of the best and most efficient receiving TEs in the league, but he has not run enough routes to reach his ceiling. That's change this year, as he's run 66% of the routes so far, which has catapulted him into the upper echelon of fantasy TEs, but his price and ownership haven't caught up. He is 3rd in the NFL in receiving yards, not amongst TEs but the entire league. He also has earned a target on 30% of his routes, and he's produced an extremely efficient 4.89 YPRR on a team high target share. The Chargers have also been an extreme pass funnel through two weeks, which plays into the Bills new high pass rate offense with the highest aDOT in the league.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Kincaid is top 5 over the last 2 seasons amongst TEs in targets per route run and fantasy points per route run, he just has never run enough rates. His route rate is now above 70% for consecutive games for the first time in his career. Absolute jam play.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: The Bills have the highest implied team total on the slate. They also rank sixth in PROE. Kincaid is Josh Allen's favorite target so far, with an elite 23.3% target share. If DJ Moore is out or limited, that should only go up. And the Chargers defense is tied for allowing the 8th-most expected points added (EPA) per pass.

players.notes: High route rate and elite targets per route run in a high total.
Consistent red-zone role and high target share.
Strong route participation and after-the-catch ability.
Expanding route rate and valuable seam targets.
